If reclamation is successful, the entire area will eventually be returned to productive use. Availability of reclaimed lands for recreational purposes will be depend upon the desires and resolutions of the surface owners. The Crow Tribe has reserved a purchase option on lands in the lease tracts.
Historical and Archaeological Sites
Any area which is expected to be disturbed by mining operations will be carefully surveyed for evidence of historical or archaeological sites.
Lease agreements include reference to the Antiquities Act of 1906. Under the terms of this Act, the destruction of historic or prehistoric ruins, monuments, or objects of antiquity without permission of the Government is prohibited.
Inadvertent destruction of historical or archaeological sites will be further minimized by instructing the equipment operators to be watchful and alert management if they should discover any evidence of a site overlooked in the survey. The reliability of this mitigating measure is probably low, due to limitations of the dragline operators field of view with respect to the overburden he is moving. Management will be responsible for notifying the proper State and Federal authorities of such evidence and appropriate assessment and salvage operations will be undertaken.
Aesthetics
Disruption of the landscape by mining activities will be mitigated by recontouring and prompt revegetation of affected lands. Planting of trees and shrubs will diversify the reclaimed landscape.
